L172: # Depth Anything 3: Recovering the Visual Space from Any Views
L173: 
L174: cite87†Haotong Lin†haotongl.github.io ^{*} · cite88†Sili Chen ^{*} · cite89†Jun Hao Liew†liewjunhao.github.io ^{*} · cite90†Donny Y. Chen†donydchen.github.io ^{*} · cite91†Zhenyu Li†zhyever.github.io · cite92†Guang Shi†scholar.google.com · cite93†Jiashi Feng†scholar.google.com.sg L175: cite94†Bingyi Kang†bingyikang.com ^{*†}
L176: 
L177: †project lead *Equal Contribution
L178: This work presents Depth Anything 3 (DA3), a model that predicts spatially consistent geometry from arbitrary visual inputs, with or without known camera poses. In pursuit of minimal modeling, DA3 yields two key insights:
L179: 
L180:   * 💎 A single plain transformer (e.g., vanilla DINO encoder) is sufficient as a backbone without architectural specialization,
L181:   * ✨ A singular depth-ray representation obviates the need for complex multi-task learning.
L182: 🏆 DA3 significantly outperforms cite95†DA2 for monocular depth estimation, and cite96†VGGT for multi-view depth estimation and pose estimation. All models are trained exclusively on public academic datasets.
L183: ## 📰 News
L184:   * 11-12-2025: 🚀 New models and cite97†DA3-Streaming released! Handle ultra-long video sequence inference with less than 12GB GPU memory via sliding-window streaming inference. Special thanks to cite98†Kai Deng for his contribution to DA3-Streaming!
L185:   * 08-12-2025: 📊 cite99†Benchmark evaluation pipeline released! Evaluate pose estimation & 3D reconstruction on 5 datasets.
L186:   * 30-11-2025: Add cite100†`use_ray_pose` and cite101†`ref_view_strategy` (reference view selection for multi-view inputs).
L187:   * 25-11-2025: Add cite102†Awesome DA3 Projects , a community-driven section featuring DA3-based applications.
L188:   * 14-11-2025: Paper, project page, code and models are all released.
L189: ## ✨ Highlights
L190: ### 🏆 Model Zoo
L191: 
L192: We release three series of models, each tailored for specific use cases in visual geometry.
L193: 
L194:   * 🌟 DA3 Main Series (`DA3-Giant`, `DA3-Large`, `DA3-Base`, `DA3-Small`) These are our flagship foundation models, trained with a unified depth-ray representation. By varying the input configuration, a single model can perform a wide range of tasks:
L195:     * 🌊 Monocular Depth Estimation: Predicts a depth map from a single RGB image.
L196:     * 🌊 Multi-View Depth Estimation: Generates consistent depth maps from multiple images for high-quality fusion.
L197:     * 🎯 Pose-Conditioned Depth Estimation: Achieves superior depth consistency when camera poses are provided as input.
L198:     * 📷 Camera Pose Estimation: Estimates camera extrinsics and intrinsics from one or more images.
L199:     * 🟡 3D Gaussian Estimation: Directly predicts 3D Gaussians, enabling high-fidelity novel view synthesis.
L200:   * 📐 DA3 Metric Series (`DA3Metric-Large`) A specialized model fine-tuned for metric depth estimation in monocular settings, ideal for applications requiring real-world scale.
L201:   * 🔍 DA3 Monocular Series (`DA3Mono-Large`). A dedicated model for high-quality relative monocular depth estimation. Unlike disparity-based models (e.g., cite95†Depth Anything 2 ), it directly predicts depth, resulting in superior geometric accuracy.
L202: 
L203: 🔗 Leveraging these available models, we developed a nested series (`DA3Nested-Giant-Large`). This series combines a any-view giant model with a metric model to reconstruct visual geometry at a real-world metric scale.
L204: ### 🛠️ Codebase Features
L205: 
L206: Our repository is designed to be a powerful and user-friendly toolkit for both practical application and future research.
L207:   * 🎨 Interactive Web UI & Gallery: Visualize model outputs and compare results with an easy-to-use Gradio-based web interface.
L208:   * ⚡ Flexible Command-Line Interface (CLI): Powerful and scriptable CLI for batch processing and integration into custom workflows.
L209:   * 💾 Multiple Export Formats: Save your results in various formats, including `glb`, `npz`, depth images, `ply`, 3DGS videos, etc, to seamlessly connect with other tools.
L210:   * 🔧 Extensible and Modular Design: The codebase is structured to facilitate future research and the integration of new models or functionalities.
L211: ## 🚀 Quick Start
L212: 
L213: ### 📦 Installation
L214: 
L215:     pip install xformers torch\>=2 torchvision
L216:     pip install -e . # Basic
L217:     pip install --no-build-isolation git+https://github.com/nerfstudio-project/gsplat.git@0b4dddf04cb687367602c01196913cde6a743d70 # for gaussian head
L218:     pip install -e ".[app]" # Gradio, python>=3.10
L219:     pip install -e ".[all]" # ALL
L220: 
L221: For detailed model information, please refer to the cite103†Model Cards section below.
L222: ### 💻 Basic Usage
L223: 
L224:     import glob, os, torch
L225:     from depth_anything_3.api import DepthAnything3
L226:     device = torch.device("cuda")
L227:     model = DepthAnything3.from_pretrained("depth-anything/DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE")
L228:     model = model.to(device=device)
L229:     example_path = "assets/examples/SOH"
L230:     images = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(example_path, "*.png")))
L231:     prediction = model.inference(
L232:         images,
L233:     )
L234:     # prediction.processed_images : [N, H, W, 3] uint8   array
L235:     print(prediction.processed_images.shape)
L236:     # prediction.depth            : [N, H, W]    float32 array
L237:     print(prediction.depth.shape)
L238:     # prediction.conf             : [N, H, W]    float32 array
L239:     print(prediction.conf.shape)
L240:     # prediction.extrinsics       : [N, 3, 4]    float32 array # opencv w2c or colmap format
L241:     print(prediction.extrinsics.shape)
L242:     # prediction.intrinsics       : [N, 3, 3]    float32 array
L243:     print(prediction.intrinsics.shape)
L244:     export MODEL_DIR=depth-anything/DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE
L245:     # This can be a Hugging Face repository or a local directory
L246:     # If you encounter network issues, consider using the following mirror: export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
L247:     # Alternatively, you can download the model directly from Hugging Face
L248:     export GALLERY_DIR=workspace/gallery
L249:     mkdir -p $GALLERY_DIR
L250: 
L251:     # CLI auto mode with backend reuse
L252:     da3 backend --model-dir ${MODEL_DIR} --gallery-dir ${GALLERY_DIR} # Cache model to gpu
L253:     da3 auto assets/examples/SOH \
L254:         --export-format glb \
L255:         --export-dir ${GALLERY_DIR}/TEST_BACKEND/SOH \
L256:         --use-backend
L257: 
L258:     # CLI video processing with feature visualization
L259:     da3 video assets/examples/robot_unitree.mp4 \
L260:         --fps 15 \
L261:         --use-backend \
L262:         --export-dir ${GALLERY_DIR}/TEST_BACKEND/robo \
L263:         --export-format glb-feat_vis \
L264:         --feat-vis-fps 15 \
L265:         --process-res-method lower_bound_resize \
L266:         --export-feat "11,21,31"
L267: 
L268:     # CLI auto mode without backend reuse
L269:     da3 auto assets/examples/SOH \
L270:         --export-format glb \
L271:         --export-dir ${GALLERY_DIR}/TEST_CLI/SOH \
L272:         --model-dir ${MODEL_DIR}
L273: The model architecture is defined in cite104†`DepthAnything3Net` , and specified with a Yaml config file located at cite105†`src/depth_anything_3/configs` . The input and output processing are handled by cite106†`DepthAnything3` . To customize the model architecture, simply create a new config file (e.g., `path/to/new/config`) as:

L276:       path: depth_anything_3.model.da3
L277:       name: DepthAnything3Net
L278:       args: as_params
L279:

L281:       __object__:
L282:         path: depth_anything_3.model.dinov2.dinov2
L283:         name: DinoV2
L284:         args: as_params
L285: 
L286:       name: vitb
L287:       out_layers: [5, 7, 9, 11]

L337: ## ❓ FAQ
L338: 
L339:   * Monocular Metric Depth: To obtain metric depth in meters from `DA3METRIC-LARGE`, use `metric_depth = focal * net_output / 300.`, where `focal` is the focal length in pixels (typically the average of fx and fy from the camera intrinsic matrix K). Note that the output from `DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE` is already in meters.
L340:   * Ray Head (`use_ray_pose`): Our API and CLI support `use_ray_pose` arg, which means that the model will derive camera pose from ray head, which is generally slightly slower, but more accurate. Note that the default is `False` for faster inference speed.
